evidence.quote:
The critical load power at Bus-15 is selected as the object
of static voltage stability analysis, that is, the load power at
Bus-15 is increased until the static stability limit is reached.
To compare the SVSA accuracy of conventional CPF and
extended CPF and to examine the impact of control parame-
ters, the following four cases are concerned:
• Case 1: SVSA based on conventional CPF where CVRPG
and SG nodes are treated as PV nodes;
• Case 2: SVSA based on extended CPF and KPi = 0.5;
• Case 3: SVSA based on extended CPF and KPi = 1.0;

evidence.quote:
In addition, this paper assumes the following:
1) The load increases with a constant power factor.
2) The active power dispatched by the synchronous generator
and VSC increases in equal proportions to the initial
benchmark value.
3) When the reactive power of the synchronous generator
or VSC exceeds the limit, the synchronous generator
rated excitation current is the maximum excitation current
that can be maintained for a long time. It is assumed
that the excitation limit is controlled by integration, and
that terminal voltage does not affect the limiting ability of
the excitation current. The VSC adopts the dq-axis current
proportional limitation method, and it is assumed that the
voltage reduction at the point of common coupling will
not affect the limiting ability of the current limitation.
4) When the synchronous generator is replaced by the VSC,
the reactive power reserve of the replacement bus will
decrease from the original QG to Q’G = (1−0.39η) QG
for kdq = 0.909 and K1 = 0.8.

Here, (1) represents a nonlinear optimization problem with

In our future work, we will combine SRSM with the sparse-
adaptive scheme to further improve the computation efﬁciency
of GSA in large-scale power system problems. Besides, we will
adopt the application of the proposed GSA method in heuristic
black-box algorithms such as artiﬁcial neural networks to the

evidence.quote:
In Table I, the sensitivities of input variables are given. For
each variable, Sy is almost equal to Ssobol , which demonstrates
the accuracy of the proposed GSA results. Sy is different from
Sloc since they belong to different categories of sensitivity anal-
ysis methods. The rankings of variables are the same for LSA
and GSA. However, there is a difference between LSA and GSA
with respect to the relative importance of variables. For exam-
ple, according to GSA, Sy of bP 9 is 0.543, which is much larger
than Sy of bP 5 and bP 7 , which means that bP 9 is signiﬁcantly
more important than bP 5 and bP 7 . However, according to LSA,
the values of Sloc for bP 5,b P 7 and bP 9 are similar. Hence, the
three variables have similar inﬂuences on the load margin.
In order to analyze the impacts of variables, let bP 5,b P 7 and
bP 9 be deterministic as the probability densities of load margins
are compared in Fig. 4. When bP 5 and bP 7 are respectively
treated as deterministic inputs, the probability distributions of
load margins are similar. When bP 9 becomes deterministic, the
probability distribution will be quite different from the other
two. This result indicates that bP 5 and bP 7 have similar impacts,
and bP 9 has a higher inﬂuence than bP 5 and bP 7 , which is
consistent with the GSA conclusion. Therefore, for independent
input variables, compared with LSA, GSA is more accurate to
describe the impacts of variables.
evidence.interpretation: GSA与局部灵敏度比较的是变量相对重要性，不是最坏点认证。

represents the system maximum loading limit. Power injection

evidence.quote:
This article first studies the static voltage stability 
indicators and related analysis and calculation methods of the 
power system. The L indicator is selected to evaluate the static 
voltage stability of the studied system. Subsequently, based on 
the static voltage stability L index, a renewable energy hosting 
capacity assessment model considering the L index was 
established. By comparing the evaluation results of the 
system's absorption capacity under different L
max settings, it 
was found that the evaluat ion results of the system's 
absorption capacity were basically positively correlated with 
the value of L
max, that is, the larger the L max value, the better 
the evaluation results of the system's absorption capacity. The 
conclusion can be achieved that when renewable energy units 
are connected to nodes with higher L index, the system's 
absorption rate and amount are higher. This conclusion can 
have certain reference value for renewable energy site 
selection.
